subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw accept `captionedFinalText` as the channel plugin API contract for fixing Telegram final-mode TTS churn in this PR?
rationale: The source fix is coherent, but adding a public channel capability that suppresses live text when enabled is a compatibility-sensitive message-delivery contract choice.

options.title: Accept the capability-gated contract
options.body: Resolve or explicitly accept the OpenGrep runner failure, then merge with Telegram as the only enabled captioned-final channel until other channels prove caption support.

options.title: Require more live proof first
options.body: Keep the PR open until tagged-mode, group-chat, or provider variations are demonstrated in a real Telegram Desktop proof on the current head.

options.title: Pause for a narrower fix
options.body: Hold this PR and ask for a Telegram-only internal fix if maintainers do not want the plugin SDK capability surface yet.

recommendation.title: Accept the capability-gated contract
recommendation.body: Resolve or explicitly accept the OpenGrep runner failure, then merge with Telegram as the only enabled captioned-final channel until other channels prove caption support.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across the reply dispatch, ACP final delivery, TTS, and channel capability surfaces touched by the contract decision.
